slides.text: Every Friday for an entire year, a shy, soft-spoken man named Leo came into my little flower shop. He always bought a single white peony, nervously clutching the delicate stem like it was made of glass. I assumed he was fiercely devoted to a beautiful girlfriend. I hated how much my heart broke every time the bell above the door chimed, secretly wishing I was the girl receiving those exquisite blooms.

On our fifty-second Friday, a torrential downpour flooded the city streets. Leo rushed in, soaking wet, his wire-rimmed glasses completely fogged up. He bought his usual peony, his hands trembling violently as he handed me a crumpled ten-dollar bill. 'She's a very lucky woman,' I finally blurted out, unable to hide the jealous, heavy ache in my chest. 'To get these beautiful flowers from you every single week.'

Leo stopped dead at the glass door. He turned around, his cheeks burning crimson beneath the rainwater. He walked slowly back to the counter and gently laid the white peony right next to my cash register. 'I don't have a girlfriend,' he whispered, looking down at his muddy shoes. 'I just... I never knew how to talk to you. I have fifty-one dead peonies sitting in my apartment.'
